page: Microsoft Azure E96ias_v4 is an isolated, memory-optimized virtual machine built on Microsoft Hyper-V. The system is driven by an AMD EPYC 7452 processor delivering 96 dedicated vCPUs across 48 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading at 3.35 GHz. The x86_64 configuration features 672.0 GB of memory (providing 7.0 GB per vCPU) and includes 1443 GB of local SSD temporary storage. Dedicated CPU allocation ensures hypervisor isolation without shared hardware contention, though it lacks hardware accelerators like GPUs and includes zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong parallel processing and memory throughput characteristics. The instance achieved top-tier performance in PassMark CPU encryption tests (96,943.13) alongside strong scores in multi-threaded bzip3 decompression (415.45 GB/sec), Clang software compilation, and overall PassMark CPU testing (68,844.02). In-memory caching operations are underscored by Redis SET performance measuring 72.45 million operations per second and small-block cached read bandwidth reaching 3,921.34 GB/sec. However, single-core execution is modest, reflected in poor stress-ng single-core rankings, and uncached large-block memory read bandwidth remains average at 162.15 GB/sec.

The primary tradeoff of the E96ias_v4 lies in its balance of raw compute per core versus dense memory capacity. Without support for advanced instructions like AVX-512 or AMX, and lacking dedicated GPU accelerators, it exhibits poor throughput for large language model inference (4.45 tokens/sec prompt processing on 70B models). Instead, resource density favors horizontally scaled multi-threaded tasks over single-threaded raw speed. This profile is well suited for large enterprise relational databases, distributed in-memory data grids, large-scale Redis caches, and memory-intensive compilation or data analytics workloads.
description: Microsoft Azure E96ias_v4 is an isolated, memory-optimized instance powered by an AMD EPYC 7452 processor. It provides 96 dedicated vCPUs across 48 physical cores running at 3.35 GHz, paired with 672.0 GB of RAM (7.0 GB per core) and 1443 GB of bundled local SSD storage. Evaluated benchmarks highlight high multi-threaded processing throughput, exceptional CPU cryptographic capabilities, and robust cached memory performance, reaching 72.45 million Redis SET operations per second and 3,921.34 GB/sec in small-block cached reads. While single-thread efficiency and large-scale model inference throughput are limited due to architecture and the absence of discrete GPUs, its dense allocation of dedicated cores and high-capacity memory makes it well suited for large in-memory caches, enterprise relational databases, big data analytics, and extensive software compilation tasks.
